headline: Energy Stands Alone as Wall Street Closes the Week on a Soft Note
body_html:
Stocks finished Friday's session on the back foot, with 340 names falling against 198 rising across our 544-stock universe. Energy was the one clear bright spot, gaining 2.65%, while consumer shares slid 1.59% and materials gave up 0.87%. Semiconductors edged up 0.18%, and software was close to flat, down 0.11%.

Moves in individual stocks were large in both directions. Staffing firm Robert Half jumped 21.74%, and Genmab and Gentherm each gained more than 9%. Cybersecurity bounced, with CrowdStrike up 8.25% and Zscaler up 7.31%, and offshore vessel operator Tidewater rose 8.11%. On the downside, Corcept Therapeutics plunged 20.13%, Bloom Energy fell 11.24%, and Credo Technology and Comfort Systems USA each lost more than 9%.

The week ahead opens Monday, October 26, with geopolitics front and center. President Trump has said another military operation against Iran is possible, and Gulf security headlines remain tense. On the data docket, economists polled by Reuters expect the Bank of Canada to raise rates to 2.50% on October 28, which keeps the focus on borrowing costs.

briefs.headline: Canada's Central Bank Expected to Tighten Again
briefs.body: A Reuters poll of economists points to the Bank of Canada lifting its policy rate to 2.50% on October 28. Respondents also expect one more increase by the end of March. The decision is the main central-bank event on the calendar this week.

briefs.headline: Iran Reportedly Eyes Gulf Undersea Cables
briefs.body: Officials say Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to strike undersea communications cables in the Gulf if fighting resumes. The report highlights how a renewed conflict could threaten data and trade links well beyond oil. Energy shares were Friday's strongest group.

briefs.headline: Washington Leaves the Door Open to More Force
briefs.body: President Trump said the US may carry out another military operation against Iran. He also said Cuba would be dealt with once the Iran situation is settled. Traders will watch Monday for any follow-through in tone or action.

briefs.headline: Saudi-Led Coalition Reports Missile Intercepts
briefs.body: The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed ballistic missiles launched by Houthi forces toward the cities of Yanbu and Taif. Yanbu is a notable Red Sea hub for the kingdom's energy exports. Any further launches could keep a risk premium in oil-linked shares.

briefs.headline: Moody's Keeps France's Credit Rating Unchanged
briefs.body: Moody's left France's sovereign rating where it was, even as the country deals with political turmoil and higher borrowing costs. The decision removes one near-term worry for European debt investors. Yields remain a point of pressure.

briefs.headline: Cyber Stocks Rebound as Selling Spreads Elsewhere
briefs.body: CrowdStrike gained 8.25% and Zscaler rose 7.31% on Friday, even as weakness spread across other parts of the market. Commentary around a bold forecast from CrowdStrike's chief executive kept security names in focus. Separately, some investors say the battered bond market is starting to offer value.
